findings.reason: The diff deletes `if (opts.flowSkipColonSpace) opts.quoteFlowKeys = true`. presenter.ts:215/223 now writes `${keyText}:${valueText}` with no space, and parser.ts:807-809 only ends a plain scalar at `:` when whitespace, end of input or a flow indicator follows, so `a:1` is read as one key with a null value. The trigger is traced: dump({a:1}, {flowLevel:0, flowSkipColonSpace:true}). I set it to high rather than critical because it only happens with an opt-in option.
findings.claim: Removing the forced quoteFlowKeys means flowSkipColonSpace emits `{a:1}`, which loads back as {"a:1": null}: the data changes silently on the round trip.
findings.evidence: The diff deletes `if (opts.flowSkipColonSpace) { opts.quoteFlowKeys = true }` from createPresenterState. It also deletes the doc comment that gave the reason: "otherwise `a:1` would be parsed as a single plain scalar instead of a mapping entry". writeFlowMapping (presenter.ts:215-223) now emits `${keyText}:${valueText}` with no separator. applyQuoteFlowKeysOption (styler_defaults.ts:33) returns early unless the user set quoteFlowKeys, so a plain key stays plain. In the parser's plain-scalar loop (parser.ts:807-809), `:` only ends the scalar when the next character is whitespace, end of input or a flow indicator. In `a:1` the next character is `1`, so `a:1` is read as one plain scalar. Nothing else in the presenter or stylers quotes the key or adds a separator, so any non-empty value whose text doesn't start with a flow indicator is affected (for example `{x: 'y'}` dumps as `{x:y}`).
